# Documentation Maintenance

## Purpose

Apply this skill whenever code is added, modified, refactored, or removed.

Documentation is part of the deliverable and must evolve with the codebase.

---

## Before Finishing Any Change

Verify the following:

### Repository Documentation

- [ ] README updated if required.
- [ ] Installation instructions remain accurate.
- [ ] Configuration documentation remains accurate.

### API Documentation

- [ ] Public API documentation updated.
- [ ] Examples updated.
- [ ] Response models updated.
- [ ] Validation rules updated.

### Architecture

- [ ] Architecture documentation updated if affected.
- [ ] Diagrams updated if affected.

### Code Documentation

- [ ] Public classes documented.
- [ ] Public methods documented.
- [ ] Comments updated where required.
- [ ] Obsolete comments removed.

### General Documentation

- [ ] Examples still work.
- [ ] Screenshots are current.
- [ ] Links are valid.
- [ ] Outdated documentation removed.

---

## Common Mistakes

Avoid:

- Updating code without updating documentation.
- Leaving obsolete examples.
- Outdated screenshots.
- Broken documentation links.
- Documentation that contradicts implementation.

---

## Definition of Done

Before considering the task complete:

- [ ] Documentation reflects the implemented solution.
- [ ] No outdated documentation remains.
- [ ] Examples remain accurate.
- [ ] Documentation changes are committed with the related code changes.
